instances.role: isolated clone of populated QA SQLite database

runtime.external_provider: none; deterministic local OpenAI-compatible SSE fixture only

observations.cli: The exact RC7 tanpopo serve --help includes --otlp-endpoint and --otlp-allow-private-ip.
observations.ssrf_policy: A startup attempt enabling private-IP access without TANPOPO_OTLP_ALLOWED_CIDRS failed closed with egress_invalid_policy. With explicit TANPOPO_OTLP_ALLOWED_CIDRS=127.0.0.1/32, the loopback collector target was permitted. This is expected protection, not a product defect.
observations.health: Both isolated runtimes returned HTTP 200 from healthz and readyz while configured to export to the loopback receiver.
observations.unauthorized_ingress: Real Chromium requested /v1/models without a bearer key: HTTP 401 invalid_virtual_key; a trace ID was returned and the receiver observed OTLP signal requests.

telemetry_receiver.kind: synthetic loopback HTTP receiver; not an OpenTelemetry Collector and does not decode protobuf
telemetry_receiver.response: HTTP 200, application/x-protobuf for each POST (receiver implementation behavior)
telemetry_receiver.privacy_limit: Canary byte absence is only a raw-byte scan of received request bodies. Since protobuf was not semantically decoded, this is not proof that no equivalent or encoded sensitive attribute was exported.

playground.journey: Owner used real Chromium Playground against the protocol-matched local OpenAI-compatible streamed fixture on the populated isolated clone.
playground.persistence: The canary request trace resolved through direct authenticated admin trace read and the Console Inspect Trace flow using the same trace ID.

observations.cleanup: Both synthetic Playground session keys were revoked; API state readback confirmed REVOKED. Screenshot: evidence/screenshots/CP61-otlp-playground-keys-revoked.png. Test runtimes were stopped. Receiver and fixture are temporary local-only test infrastructure.

classification.DEF-063: PASS (scoped): exact RC7 runtime exposes configurable OTLP endpoint and sent trace data to the configured loopback endpoint. Historical RC6 failure remains preserved; real OTel collector compatibility and other deployments remain unverified.
classification.DEF-064: PASS (scoped): exact RC7 runtime emitted OTLP protobuf HTTP posts to all three observed signal paths: traces, metrics, and logs. Semantic decoding, a real collector/export backend, delivery retry/backpressure, persistent exporter failure, and metric/log semantics remain unverified.
classification.privacy: PARTIAL: no raw canary byte sequences were present; protobuf semantic content and broader data classes were not decoded or verified.
classification.security_policy: PASS (scoped): private loopback export remained blocked absent an explicit allowed CIDR and worked after explicit 127.0.0.1/32 authorization.
limitations: The receiver is a synthetic sink that returns 200 and does not validate protobuf wire semantics or collector interoperability.
The 1-second metrics interval was intentionally used to make metrics observable and generated a high request count; this does not represent default operational volume.
No Windows/macOS deployment, remote collector, TLS/mTLS, authentication, outage/retry, buffering, or production egress behavior was tested.
Historical defect reports and results remain retained; these current scoped outcomes do not globally close either defect.
